the_sentence: (d) These rights are intended to operate within the framework of the Companies Act, 2013, and shall, to the extent required, be incorporated into the Articles of Association of the Company; in the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Articles as between the Shareholders, this Agreement shall prevail and the Shareholders shall procure amendment of the Articles accordingly.
a_correction_to_an_earlier_statement: In the D4.44 conversation the term-sheet version of this sentence was described as stating the opposite of Indian law. That was too strong. The sentence is limited to the position 'as between the Shareholders' and pairs it with an obligation to amend the Articles, which is a common construction in Indian shareholders' agreements. The questions below are what decides whether it works; engineering cannot decide them.
what_it_governs: the board composition and the Investor's right to nominate a director
a quorum that requires an Investor Director
Reserved Matters: an Investor veto over listed company actions, said to apply 'notwithstanding any other provision'
precedence of the agreement over the Articles 'as between the Shareholders', and an obligation on the Shareholders to procure amendment of the Articles
questions_for_the_advocate: Is the Company itself a party to the SHA and the SSA as generated, and if not, which of these rights can bind the Company before the Articles are amended?

Does the answer differ for a private company (Articles restrict transfer under Companies Act 2013 s.2(68)) and a public company (s.58(2) proviso: a contract between two or more persons on transfer of securities is enforceable as a contract)?

For each right listed above — board nomination, quorum, Reserved Matters veto, information rights — is an inter se precedence clause effective between the signing shareholders, and what is the position of a shareholder who has not signed?
Should the SHA and SSA instead (or also) make the Articles amendment a condition precedent to completion, so the rights are in the Articles from the outset?
Is the 'notwithstanding any other provision' veto consistent with directors' duties (s.166) and with the statutory powers of the Board and of the general meeting that cannot be delegated or fettered?
Does s.6 (the Act overrides the Memorandum, the Articles and any agreement to the extent of repugnancy) require any qualification in the clause?
Approve, amend or replace sub-clause (d), separately for the SHA and the SSA.

authorities_to_verify.point: the Act overrides the Memorandum, Articles and agreements to the extent repugnant
a private company's Articles restrict the right to transfer its shares
contracts between two or more persons in respect of transfer of securities (of a public company) are enforceable as contracts

authorities_to_verify.authority: V.B. Rangaraj v. V.B. Gopalakrishnan, (1992) 1 SCC 160
authorities_to_verify.point: a restriction on share transfer not contained in the Articles does not bind the company or its shareholders

authorities_to_verify.authority: Later decisions qualifying Rangaraj (for example Messer Holdings v. Shyam Madanmohan Ruia, Bombay High Court; Vodafone International Holdings v. Union of India, (2012) 6 SCC 613; World Phone India v. WPI Group, Delhi High Court)
authorities_to_verify.point: listed as leads only; their holdings and citations must be confirmed by the advocate before anything relies on them
